requirements.original: The value of the local verdict may be retrieved using the getverdict operation.
requirements.canonical: The value of the local verdict MAY be retrieved using the `getverdict` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 24.3 -- The value of the local verdict may be retrieved using the getverdict operation.

requirements.original: getverdict
requirements.canonical: The `getverdict` operation has the syntax `getverdict` (the keyword alone, without parentheses or arguments).

examples.text: v_myResult := getverdict; // Where v_myResult is a variable of type verdicttype

requirements.header: // @requirement: 24.3 -- getverdict

requirements.original: The getverdict operation returns the actual value of the local verdict.
requirements.canonical: The `getverdict` operation IS returning the actual value of the local verdict as a `verdicttype` value.

examples.text: v_myResult := getverdict; // Where v_myResult is a variable of type verdicttype

requirements.header: // @requirement: 24.3 -- The getverdict operation returns the actual value of the local verdict.

requirements.original: Items to be displayed shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the action statement.
requirements.canonical: An item to be displayed by the `action` statement SHALL be identified in a comma-separated list in the argument of the `action` statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 25 -- Items to be displayed shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the action statement.

requirements.original: Items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such items.
requirements.canonical: An item of the `action` statement MAY be an individual language element specified in table 18 or an expression composed of such items.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax (25-s006) only allows FreeText or TemplateInstance, while table 18 (log statement) also lists elements such as timers, ports and component references; it is unclear whether all table 18 elements are allowed in `action`. Chosen reading: the elements of table 18 are allowed.
readings: An item of the `action` statement MAY be any language element listed in table 18 or an expression composed of such elements.
An item of the `action` statement MAY only be a free text or a template instance, as given by the syntactical structure.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 25 -- Items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such items.

requirements.original: action "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")"
requirements.canonical: The `action` statement has the syntax `action` "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 25 -- action "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")"

requirements.original: External actions can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.canonical: The `action` statement MAY be used in testcases, functions and altsteps.

ambiguity.issue: The list omits the module control function, although table 16 and clause 26 allow `action` in control behaviour. Chosen reading: the list is not exhaustive. Also "test cases" is used where "testcases" (the language element) is meant.
readings: The `action` statement MAY be used in testcases, functions, altsteps and the module control function.
The `action` statement MAY be used only in testcases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 25 -- External actions can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.original: Test cases are defined in the module definitions part while the control functions manage their execution.
requirements.canonical: A test case IS defined in the module definitions part.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.0 -- Test cases are defined in the module definitions part while the control functions manage their execution.

requirements.canonical: An assignment (`:=`) MAY be used in control behaviour.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.0 -- Statement: Label and Goto; Associated keyword or symbol: label / goto

requirements.canonical: The `stop` statement (stop execution) MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.0 -- Statement: Stop execution; Associated keyword or symbol: stop

requirements.canonical: The `break` statement (leaving a loop, alt or interleave) MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.0 -- Statement: Leaving a loop, alt or interleave; Associated keyword or symbol: break

requirements.original: Test cases are executed with an execute statement in the module control.
requirements.canonical: A test case IS executed by an `execute` statement in the module control function.

ambiguity.issue: "module control" is used instead of the V4.17.1 term "module control function".

examples.text:
execute(TC_MyTestCase1()); // executes TC_MyTestCase1, without storing the
                   // returned test verdict and without time supervision

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Test cases are executed with an execute statement in the module control.

requirements.original: execute "(" TestcaseRef "(" [ { ActualPar [","] } ] ")" [ "," TimerValue [ "," HostId ] ] ")"
requirements.canonical: The `execute` statement has the syntax `execute ( TestcaseRef ( [ActualPar {, ActualPar}] ) [, TimerValue [, HostId]] )`.

examples.text:
execute(TC_MyTestCase1()); // executes TC_MyTestCase1, without storing the
                   // returned test verdict and without time supervision

v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase2()); // executes TC_MyTestCase2 and stores the resulting
                             // verdict in variable v_myVerdict

v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase3(), -, "Host1");
  // executes TC_MyTestCase3 with unlimited time with MTC deployed to 'Host1'

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- execute "(" TestcaseRef "(" [ { ActualPar [","] } ] ")" [ "," TimerValue [ "," HostId ] ] ")"

requirements.original: The execute statement is used to start test cases (see clause 27.1) in control behaviour.
requirements.canonical: The `execute` statement IS used to start a test case in control behaviour.

ambiguity.issue: The cross-reference "see clause 27.1" points to the attribute mechanism, which is unrelated; clause 16.3 (Test cases) is most likely meant. The reading with clause 16.3 is used.
readings: The `execute` statement IS used to start a test case (as defined in clause 16.3) in control behaviour.
The `execute` statement IS used to start a test case in control behaviour, with attribute rules of clause 27.1 applying.

examples.text:
execute(TC_MyTestCase1()); // executes TC_MyTestCase1, without storing the
                   // returned test verdict and without time supervision

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- The execute statement is used to start test cases (see clause 27.1) in control behaviour.

requirements.original: The result of an executed test case is always a value of type verdicttype.
requirements.canonical: The result of an `execute` statement IS always a value of type `verdicttype`.

examples.text:
v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase2()); // executes TC_MyTestCase2 and stores the resulting
                             // verdict in variable v_myVerdict

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- The result of an executed test case is always a value of type verdicttype.

requirements.original: Every test case shall contain one and only one MTC the type of which is referenced in the header of the test case definition.
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL contain exactly one MTC.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Every test case shall contain one and only one MTC the type of which is referenced in the header of the test case definition.

requirements.original: Every test case shall contain one and only one MTC the type of which is referenced in the header of the test case definition.
requirements.canonical: The MTC of a test case IS of the component type referenced in the header (`runs on` clause) of the test case definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Every test case shall contain one and only one MTC the type of which is referenced in the header of the test case definition.

requirements.original: The behaviour defined in the test case body is the behaviour of the MTC.
requirements.canonical: The behaviour defined in the test case body IS the behaviour of the MTC.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- The behaviour defined in the test case body is the behaviour of the MTC.

requirements.original: When a test case is invoked the MTC is created, the ports of the MTC and the test system interface are instantiated and the behaviour specified in the test case definition is started on the MTC.
requirements.canonical: When a test case is invoked, the MTC IS created.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- When a test case is invoked the MTC is created, the ports of the MTC and the test system interface are instantiated and the behaviour specified in the test case definition is started on the MTC.

requirements.original: When a test case is invoked the MTC is created, the ports of the MTC and the test system interface are instantiated and the behaviour specified in the test case definition is started on the MTC.
requirements.canonical: When a test case is invoked, the ports of the MTC and of the test system interface ARE instantiated.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- When a test case is invoked the MTC is created, the ports of the MTC and the test system interface are instantiated and the behaviour specified in the test case definition is started on the MTC.

requirements.original: When a test case is invoked the MTC is created, the ports of the MTC and the test system interface are instantiated and the behaviour specified in the test case definition is started on the MTC.
requirements.canonical: When a test case is invoked, the behaviour specified in the test case definition IS started on the MTC.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- When a test case is invoked the MTC is created, the ports of the MTC and the test system interface are instantiated and the behaviour specified in the test case definition is started on the MTC.

requirements.original: All these actions shall be performed implicitly i.e. without explicit create and start operations.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 tool SHALL create the MTC, instantiate the ports of the MTC and the test system interface, and start the test case behaviour on the MTC implicitly, without explicit `create` and `start` operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- All these actions shall be performed implicitly i.e. without explicit create and start operations.

requirements.original: As the result of the execution of a test case, a test case verdict of either none, pass, inconc, fail or error shall be returned and may be assigned to a variable for further processing.
requirements.canonical: The `execute` statement SHALL return a test case verdict of `none`, `pass`, `inconc`, `fail` or `error` as the result of the execution of the test case.

examples.text:
v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase2()); // executes TC_MyTestCase2 and stores the resulting
                             // verdict in variable v_myVerdict

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- As the result of the execution of a test case, a test case verdict of either none, pass, inconc, fail or error shall be returned and may be assigned to a variable for further processing.

requirements.original: As the result of the execution of a test case, a test case verdict of either none, pass, inconc, fail or error shall be returned and may be assigned to a variable for further processing.
requirements.canonical: The verdict returned by an `execute` statement MAY be assigned to a variable.

examples.text:
v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase2()); // executes TC_MyTestCase2 and stores the resulting
                             // verdict in variable v_myVerdict

execute(TC_MyTestCase1()); // executes TC_MyTestCase1, without storing the
                   // returned test verdict and without time supervision

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- As the result of the execution of a test case, a test case verdict of either none, pass, inconc, fail or error shall be returned and may be assigned to a variable for further processing.

requirements.original: Optionally, the execute statement allows supervision of a test case by means of a timer duration.
requirements.canonical: An `execute` statement MAY specify a timer duration (TimerValue) to supervise the execution of the test case.

examples.text:
execute(TC_MyTestCase1()); // executes TC_MyTestCase1, without storing the
                   // returned test verdict and without time supervision

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Optionally, the execute statement allows supervision of a test case by means of a timer duration.

requirements.original: Also optionally, the execute statement allows deployment of the MTC to a specific host before starting the execution.
requirements.canonical: An `execute` statement MAY specify a host to which the MTC is deployed before the execution of the test case starts.

examples.text:
v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase3(), -, "Host1");
  // executes TC_MyTestCase3 with unlimited time with MTC deployed to 'Host1'

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Also optionally, the execute statement allows deployment of the MTC to a specific host before starting the execution.

requirements.original: All variables (if any) visible in the scope unit where the execute statement is used shall be passed into the test case by parameterization if they are to be used in the behaviour definition of that test case, i.e. TTCN-3 does not support global variables of any kind.
requirements.canonical: A variable visible in the scope unit of an `execute` statement SHALL be passed to the test case as an actual parameter if it is to be used in the behaviour definition of that test case.
requirements.condition: the variable is to be used in the behaviour definition of the test case
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- All variables (if any) visible in the scope unit where the execute statement is used shall be passed into the test case by parameterization if they are to be used in the behaviour definition of that test case, i.e. TTCN-3 does not support global variables of any kind.

requirements.original: All variables (if any) visible in the scope unit where the execute statement is used shall be passed into the test case by parameterization if they are to be used in the behaviour definition of that test case, i.e. TTCN-3 does not support global variables of any kind.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language does NOT support global variables of any kind.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- All variables (if any) visible in the scope unit where the execute statement is used shall be passed into the test case by parameterization if they are to be used in the behaviour definition of that test case, i.e. TTCN-3 does not support global variables of any kind.

requirements.original: At the start of each test case, the test configuration shall be reset.
requirements.canonical: The test configuration SHALL be reset at the start of each test case.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- At the start of each test case, the test configuration shall be reset.

requirements.original: This means that all components and ports conducted by create, connect, etc. operations in a previous test case were destroyed when that test case was stopped (hence are not "visible" to the new test case).
requirements.canonical: A test component or port created or connected (by `create`, `connect`, etc. operations) in a previous test case IS destroyed when that test case is stopped and IS NOT visible to a subsequent test case.

ambiguity.issue: "conducted" is used for components and ports set up by create/connect/map operations; "created" (components) and "connected/mapped" (ports) is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- This means that all components and ports conducted by create, connect, etc. operations in a previous test case were destroyed when that test case was stopped (hence are not "visible" to the new test case).

requirements.original: A test case terminates with the termination of the MTC.
requirements.canonical: A test case terminates when its MTC terminates.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- A test case terminates with the termination of the MTC.

requirements.original: On termination of the MTC (explicitly or implicitly), all running parallel test components shall be removed by the test system.
requirements.canonical: When the MTC terminates (explicitly or implicitly), the test system SHALL remove all running PTCs.
requirements.condition: the MTC terminates explicitly or implicitly
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- On termination of the MTC (explicitly or implicitly), all running parallel test components shall be removed by the test system.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Statement: Next iteration of a loop; Associated keyword or symbol: continue

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Statement: Stop timer; Associated keyword or symbol: stop

requirements.canonical: The `action` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Statement: Stimulate an (SUT) action externally; Associated keyword or symbol: action

requirements.canonical: The `execute` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Statement: Execute test case; Associated keyword or symbol: execute

requirements.original: The final verdict of a test case is calculated based on the final local verdicts of the different test components according to the rules defined in clause 24.1.
requirements.canonical: The final verdict of a test case IS calculated from the final local verdicts of the test components according to the rules of clause 24.1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- The final verdict of a test case is calculated based on the final local verdicts of the different test components according to the rules defined in clause 24.1.

requirements.original: The actual local verdict of a test component becomes its final local verdict when the test component terminates itself or is stopped by itself, another test component or by the test system.
requirements.canonical: The actual local verdict of a test component becomes its final local verdict when the test component terminates itself or is stopped by itself, by another test component or by the test system.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- The actual local verdict of a test component becomes its final local verdict when the test component terminates itself or is stopped by itself, another test component or by the test system.

requirements.original: Timer may be used to supervise the execution of a test case.
requirements.canonical: The execution of a test case MAY be supervised by a timer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- Timer may be used to supervise the execution of a test case.

requirements.original: This may be done using an explicit timeout in the execute statement.
requirements.canonical: Test case supervision IS done by an explicit timeout (TimerValue) in the `execute` statement.

ambiguity.issue: "may" can be read as a permission (one possible way, others exist) or as a description of the only mechanism; the execute statement timeout is the only mechanism defined, so the descriptive reading is used.
readings: Test case supervision IS done by an explicit timeout (TimerValue) in the `execute` statement.
Test case supervision MAY be done by an explicit timeout in the `execute` statement or by other means.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- This may be done using an explicit timeout in the execute statement.

requirements.original: If the test case does not end within this duration, the result of the test case execution shall be an error verdict and the test system shall terminate the test case.
requirements.canonical: If the test case does not end within the supervision duration, the result of the `execute` statement SHALL be the verdict `error`.
requirements.condition: the test case does not end within the duration given by the TimerValue of the execute statement
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- If the test case does not end within this duration, the result of the test case execution shall be an error verdict and the test system shall terminate the test case.

requirements.original: If the test case does not end within this duration, the result of the test case execution shall be an error verdict and the test system shall terminate the test case.
requirements.canonical: If the test case does not end within the supervision duration, the test system SHALL terminate the test case.
requirements.condition: the test case does not end within the duration given by the TimerValue of the execute statement
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- If the test case does not end within this duration, the result of the test case execution shall be an error verdict and the test system shall terminate the test case.

requirements.canonical: The test case supervision timer NEED NOT be declared or started.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- The timer used for test case supervision is a system timer and need not be declared or started.
